clue.text: Difficult situation in which the Turkish bather finds himself

definitions.text: Difficult situation in which the Turkish bather finds himself

blocks.note: surface reading: a tricky predicament someone is put in

blocks.clueFragment: in which the Turkish bather finds himself
blocks.note: setter's reading: a man in a steam room sits on a very warm bench

explanation.walkthrough: A Turkish bath is a steam bath, so the bather literally sits somewhere scorching; the phrase also means being under intense pressure to answer or decide.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a position of uncomfortable responsibility or questioning, such as a contestant facing the quizmaster.

clue.text: Release is but a beggarly gesture

blocks.note: first meaning: a press statement given out to journalists
second meaning: a small gift of charity to someone in need

explanation.surface: Setting someone free is only a mean, grudging act.
explanation.walkthrough: Release looks like a verb; it is the noun for an official statement, a press release.
explanation.definitionFit: A handout is both a printed statement distributed to the press and alms given to the poor.

clue.text: Was it all the rage among the citizens of Babel?

definitions.text: Was it all the rage among the citizens of Babel?

blocks.note: surface reading: was it fashionable
setter's reading: the people of Babel were obsessed with building a tall structure, and rage means fury

explanation.walkthrough: The Biblical people of Babel built a tower to reach heaven; an enthusiasm for towers is literally a 'towering' passion, and the phrase means extreme anger.
explanation.definitionFit: A towering passion is a fit of violent fury, so it is rage at its height.

clue.text: Ireland's inner vivacity

indicators.note: inner points to the letters lying inside the name of the country rather than at its edges

blocks.note: the middle letters of the country's name

explanation.surface: The Irish have a liveliness deep within them.
explanation.definitionFit: Élan is French-derived for dash and energetic style, close in sense to liveliness.

clue.text: They make lace from rags

blocks.note: first meaning: people who do tatting, a knotted lacework
second meaning: torn shreds of cloth

explanation.surface: Lacemakers fashion their work out of old scraps of cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: Tatting is handmade lace knotted with a shuttle, so its makers are tatters.
explanation.definitionFit: Tatters are ragged torn pieces of fabric, and those who tat lace are also tatters.

clue.text: A pessimist is a useless Fellow

blocks.note: first meaning: someone who has given up expecting anything good
second meaning: a person with no chance of success

explanation.walkthrough: The capital F on Fellow is just the printing; it is the ordinary word for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: The informal noun describes a hopeless case, and read literally it is one without hope, which suits a gloomy person.

clue.text: Want to be guided or goaded?

blocks.note: to want something is to need it
guided means led

explanation.surface: Would you rather be steered gently or prodded along?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guided or goaded' looks like a choice between two definitions; only the second is one.
explanation.definitionFit: To needle someone is to provoke or prod them, so needled means goaded.

clue.text: Judge Jeffreys's favourite expletive?

blocks.note: surface reading: a mild oath, as in 'confound it'
setter's reading: the notorious seventeenth-century judge sent hundreds to the gallows

explanation.walkthrough: Judge Jeffreys presided over the Bloody Assizes of 1685 and is remembered as the hanging judge; 'hang it!' is a mild oath.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an old-fashioned exclamation of annoyance and also the sentence such a judge loved to pass.

clue.text: Carry out suggestion to aspiring GP with money to invest

definitions.text: suggestion to aspiring GP with money to invest

blocks.note: first meaning: to apply a plan in real life

blocks.clueFragment: suggestion to aspiring GP with money to invest
blocks.note: second meaning: advice to sink cash into a medical partnership

explanation.surface: Acting on financial advice given to a would-be family doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: A GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor, whose surgery is called a practice; new GPs once bought into one.
explanation.definitionFit: To put a plan into practice is to implement it, which is what carrying it out means.

clue.text: Modify plans for conscription of sappers

blocks.note: the Royal Engineers, the British Army's sappers, are the RE
the draft is the call-up of soldiers

explanation.surface: Changing the arrangements for calling up military engineers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Conscription of sappers' is read as the sappers' draft, so their letters come first.
explanation.definitionFit: To redraft is to write a new version of a plan or document, which modifies it.

clue.text: Young Barbara joined the football team

blocks.note: young things are new
Barbara Castle was a prominent Labour cabinet minister
joined together means united

explanation.surface: A girl called Barbara signs up with a football club.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Castle was a well-known British Labour politician of the 1960s and 70s. NEWCASTLE UNITED is an English Premier League football club from the north-east.
explanation.definitionFit: The answer is the name of a professional football club based in Newcastle upon Tyne, so it is one particular team.

clue.text: Proprietorial claim reveals sour disposition

indicators.note: a disposition is also an arrangement, so the preceding word has its letters set out afresh

blocks.note: taken as written, four letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone staking a claim to property shows a bitter temperament.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sour disposition' reads as a grumpy nature; disposition here means placing in order.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying 'it is ours' asserts possession, so the possessive pronoun is itself an owner's claim.

clue.text: Greeting conveyed by infernal cipher

blocks.note: the infernal regions are hell
a cipher is a zero, which looks like the letter O

explanation.surface: A salutation is sent in a fiendish secret code.
explanation.walkthrough: Cipher wants to mean a code; its older sense is nought, the figure 0.
explanation.definitionFit: The everyday word said on meeting someone or answering the phone is a standard greeting.

clue.text: Rank wartime entertainer

blocks.note: surface reading: an entertainer in uniform with a military rank
setter's reading: rank means foul, the Second World War troop-show body nicknamed Every Night Something Awful

explanation.walkthrough: ENSA, the Entertainments National Service Association, put on shows for British forces in the Second World War, and its quality was so mocked that troops expanded the initials as 'Every Night Something Awful'.
explanation.definitionFit: The organisation supplied performers to the armed forces during the war, so it was the wartime entertainer of the troops.

clue.text: Monumental stupidity

blocks.note: surface reading: enormous; setter's reading: in the form of a monument
a foolish act, and also a useless ornamental tower built on a country estate

explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a folly is a whimsical decorative building, often a mock ruin, put up on a landed estate for show.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means foolishness, and also an extravagant purposeless structure, a monument to foolishness.

clue.text: Film a second-rate Shakespearean drama

blocks.note: B is the grade below A, second class
King Lear is a Shakespeare tragedy

explanation.surface: A poor-quality movie of one of the Bard's plays.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Film' looks like a movie, but it is the verb for clouding over, as eyes blur.
explanation.definitionFit: To blear is to dim the eyes or a view, as a thin film of moisture over the eye does.

clue.text: They're muscular cricketing fellows but one man short

blocks.note: a cricket side has eleven players, and with the qualifier that follows this count drops by one
fellows of a university college are dons
qualifies the cricketing side: it is a player down, which fixes the count of the first piece

explanation.surface: Brawny cricketers take the field with a player missing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fellows' looks like part of the cricket team, but it supplies a separate piece: dons, the senior members of an Oxford or Cambridge college.
explanation.definitionFit: Tendons are the tough cords joining muscle to bone, so they belong to the muscular system.

clue.text: Distribute unemployment benefit when on strike

blocks.note: the dole is British slang for unemployment pay
strikers are said to be out

explanation.surface: Handing out jobless money to workers who have walked out.
explanation.walkthrough: Being 'on the dole' is British for living on unemployment benefit; 'all out' is the strikers' call.
explanation.definitionFit: To dole something out is to share it out in portions, which is to distribute it.

clue.text: Spotted fruit in divine setting

indicators.note: in places the fruit within the letters for the clergyman
a setting holds a jewel round its edges, so the divine wraps around the fruit

blocks.note: DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the abbreviation for a divine, a clergyman
an apple is a fruit

explanation.surface: Speckled fruit sits in some heavenly surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: A divine is a theologian or priest, hence his degree letters DD; they split to set the fruit between them.
explanation.definitionFit: Dappled describes a coat or surface marked with patches of a different shade, so it means spotted.

clue.text: Sid and I treated with contempt

indicators.note: treated means processed or worked on, so the letters before it are remade

blocks.note: taken as written, seven letters

explanation.surface: Two friends were snubbed and looked down on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Treated with contempt' reads as one phrase meaning scorned; it splits, and only the last word is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Disdain is the feeling that someone is beneath one's notice, a synonym of scorn.

clue.text: Bore in the German visionary

indicators.note: in places the first word inside the German article that follows

blocks.note: der is a German word for the
to ream is to bore out or widen a hole

explanation.surface: A tedious person lives inside the German idealist.
explanation.walkthrough: Bore looks like a dull person; it is the verb to drill.
explanation.definitionFit: A dreamer is someone with grand imaginative ideas, which is what a visionary is.

clue.text: Boxed calcite and ruby

blocks.note: Iceland spar is a clear form of calcite, and spar is a general name for such crystals
ruby is a shade of red

explanation.surface: Mineral specimens and a gemstone packed in a case.
explanation.walkthrough: Boxed looks like packaged, but it is the past tense of boxing in the ring.
explanation.definitionFit: To spar is to practise boxing with punches, so sparred is the past tense meaning boxed.

clue.text: Reel showing film celebrity swallowing egg-flip

indicators.note: to flip something is to turn it over, so the word joined to it runs backwards
what swallows takes the other piece inside itself

blocks.note: a famous film actor is a star
taken as written

explanation.surface: A movie star gulps down an eggnog-style drink and staggers about.
explanation.walkthrough: An egg-flip is a real drink, eggnog, which makes the surface convincing; reel is the verb to sway.
explanation.definitionFit: To reel is to walk unsteadily, lurching from side to side, which is to stagger.

clue.text: A downtrodden person on the threshold

definitions.note: a description of where the mat lies, not a noun

blocks.note: first meaning: someone others walk all over
second meaning: the mat laid at the entrance to a house

explanation.surface: An oppressed person is standing at the door.
explanation.walkthrough: The joke is that the mat is literally trodden down, at the doorway.
explanation.definitionFit: A doormat is a mat at the entrance for wiping feet, and figuratively a submissive person who is exploited.

clue.text: Indifferent response to two appeals

blocks.note: surface reading: a shrug when asked how something went
setter's reading: the reply looks like the distress call SOS sent twice, clipped

explanation.walkthrough: The (2-2) answer reads as two shortened copies of the distress signal, the 'appeals' for help, but it is the word for middling.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something was 'so-so' means it was only mediocre, neither good nor bad, a lukewarm verdict.

clue.text: Badly cared for timber

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters that follow come out in the wrong order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Wood that has been neglected.
explanation.definitionFit: Cedar is a fragrant softwood used for chests and pencils, an example of timber.

clue.text: A sound comeback from one with a narcissistic passion

definitions.text: A sound comeback from one with a narcissistic passion

blocks.note: surface reading: a good retort; setter's reading: a reflected noise

blocks.clueFragment: from one with a narcissistic passion
blocks.note: in Greek myth the nymph who loved Narcissus pined until only her voice remained

explanation.walkthrough: 'Narcissistic' looks like vanity, but it means 'for Narcissus': the nymph Echo loved him and faded to a voice that repeats others.
explanation.definitionFit: An echo is a sound that bounces back, and the nymph Echo is the lover of Narcissus in Ovid's story.

clue.text: The bulk of graduates get a second

blocks.note: Masters of Arts are MAs
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: Most university leavers come away with a second-class degree.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'second' is a British degree grade, which makes the surface plausible.
explanation.definitionFit: The mass of something is its main body or majority, the same as the bulk.

clue.text: Fingered soft fabric

blocks.note: first meaning: touched with the hands
second meaning: a matted woollen cloth

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as a description of handling cloth; the two halves are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Felt is the past tense of feel, to touch, and also a cloth made by pressing wool fibres together.

clue.text: Mating males' main attribute

blocks.note: setter's reading: beasts in the breeding season, hence the bestial adjective
surface reading: the quality that wins a partner, sexual charm

explanation.walkthrough: As a bonus, the letters of 'mating males main' rearrange exactly into the answer, though no word signals it.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means raw personal attractiveness to the opposite sex, the pull a suitor most needs.

clue.text: One who doesn't employ a neglected legal entitlement

definitions.text: One who doesn't employ a neglected legal entitlement

blocks.note: surface reading: someone with no staff
setter's reading: in law, failing to exercise a right can forfeit it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Employ' wants to mean hire workers; here it means use, as a right is used.
explanation.definitionFit: A person who fails to make use of something is literally a non-user, and nonuser is also the legal term for neglecting a right.

clue.text: It is beaten by a beaten army

definitions.text: It is beaten by a beaten army

blocks.note: setter's reading: a drum signal that is sounded
surface reading: troops who have lost the battle and must withdraw

explanation.walkthrough: The two senses of 'beaten' are played against each other: drummed and defeated. Armies once signalled withdrawal by beating a drum.
explanation.definitionFit: A defeated army falls back, and the idiom 'beat a retreat' comes from the drum call ordering that withdrawal.
